#PPOD: Going the Distance on Mars 🔴 @NASAPersevere has made history! On October 11, 2026, the rover reached a total distance of 45.22 kilometers across #Mars, surpassing the 45.16-kilometer record set by its predecessor, Opportunity. This Navcam image captures Perseverance's tracks stretching across the Martian terrain during the drive that made it the farthest-traveling vehicle on another world. Since landing in Jezero Crater in February 2021, Perseverance has explored ancient lakebed sediments, collected rock samples, and climbed toward the crater's rim in search of clues to Mars's watery past. Its autonomous navigation system, AutoNav, lets the rover identify obstacles and plan routes with less guidance from Earth, helping it cover more ground across challenging terrain. With new geological targets ahead, Perseverance's record-breaking journey is far from over. Credit: @NASA @NASAJPL @Caltech #planetaryscience

I asked Opus 5.5 to give me the top 10 critical points! 0. "a country of geniuses in a data center" Anthropic says it is working toward Claude handling open-ended tasks that last days or weeks, with millions of AI “Virtual Collaborators” running in parallel. The filing calls the end result “a country of geniuses in a data center,” available to every organization. 1. The growth curve Anthropic's revenue went from $41M in 2023 to $386M in 2024 to $4.59B in 2025, and hit $16.3B in just the first half of 2026, versus $1.16B in H1 2025. That's about 14x year over year. 2. Customers keep spending more Net Revenue Retention was roughly 900% as of Sept 30, 2026. On average, existing customers are spending about 9x what they spent a year ago. For context, strong SaaS companies usually report 110–130%. 3. Big customers As of Sept 30, 2026, over 11,900 customers spent $100K+, over 1,900 spent $1M+, and about 250 spent $10M+ on a trailing-twelve-month basis. 4. Revenue is growing faster than compute costs In Q2 2026, revenue grew 1,368% year over year while compute and infrastructure expenses grew 300%. That gap is the core of the bull case. 5. Profitable on an adjusted basis Adjusted operating income flipped from a $4.85B loss in 2025 to a $1.6B profit in H1 2026, a 10% adjusted margin. On a GAAP basis, the operating loss narrowed from $8.06B to $693M. 6. The $80B loss explained The H1 2026 net loss was $80.7B, but $72.4B of it came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes and similar instruments, driven mostly by the company's rising valuation. In other words, much of the loss is non-cash and comes from the company being worth more. 7. Revenue per employee Trailing-twelve-month revenue per employee was over $6.6M as of Sept 2026, up from $1.4M a year earlier. The company says this is partly because its teams use Claude extensively in their own work. 8. Anthropic’s AGI-style prediction The S-1 says Anthropic expects “Powerful AI” to be widely available within a few years. It describes this as AI that matches or beats top human experts in most professional and scientific fields, can work on its own for hours, days, or weeks, coordinates with other AI systems, and can operate lab equipment and robots. 9. Equity set aside for public benefit Anthropic put 5% of its fully diluted shares into a Public Benefit Fund. The board can add up to another 2% each time the stock rises 50% above its previous milestone, and each co-founder has pledged 80% of their personal equity to philanthropy. 10. A notable risk factor The filing warns that using Claude to build future Claude models could make capabilities advance faster than safety measures can keep up. It also says the company has delayed or limited releases before, citing Mythos and Project Glasswing, and may do so again even if it hurts competitiveness. Bonus: Anthropic has raised $141.1B in total and held about $131.7B in cash and short-term investments as of June 30, 2026. Sales and marketing spending jumped from $120M in H1 2025 to $3.17B in H1 2026. NASA engineers used Claude Code to plan the first AI-planned drive of the Mars Perseverance rover.

Résumé de l’actualité spatiale du 19 au 25 octobre Lundi 19 octobre Une fusée japonaise H3-24L a décollé à 21h41 (heure de Paris) depuis le pas de tir LA-Y2, à #Tanegashima, au Japon, dans le cadre de la mission #MMX. Sous sa coiffe se trouvait la sonde #MMX, accompagnée du petit rover franco-allemand #IDEFIX. La mission a pour objectif d’explorer Phobos, l’une des deux lunes de Mars. L’arrivée de la sonde dans l’environnement martien est prévue pour 2027. Mardi 20 octobre Une fusée #Falcon9 de @SpaceX a décollé à 13h04 (heure de Paris) depuis le complexe de lancement SLC-40, à Cap Canaveral, en Floride, pour la mission Bandwagon-5. Sous sa coiffe se trouvaient 31 petits satellites ainsi qu’une capsule Starfall. @elonmusk a confirmé que @SpaceX prévoyait de tenter de récupérer simultanément le vaisseau Ship 42 et le booster B22 lors de l'IFT-15. Celui-ci pourrait avoir lieu en novembre, au plus tôt. Mercredi 21 octobre L’entreprise espagnole @PLD_Space a annoncé avoir construit trois exemplaires de son lanceur #Miura5. Les premiers essais sont attendus l’année prochaine en Guyane française. Jeudi 22 octobre Dans un document #CADENA, @blueorigin a indiqué que le prochain vol de sa fusée New Glenn pourrait avoir lieu le 28 décembre, au plus tôt. Vendredi 23 octobre Une fusée #Electron de @RocketLab a décollé à 09h11 (heure de Paris) depuis le pas de tir LC-1A, dans le cadre de la mission HawkEye 360 Cluster 16. Sous sa coiffe se trouvaient trois satellites destinés à la constellation #HawkEye360, développés pour le compte de l’entreprise #HawkEye360, avec le soutien du #SpaceFlightLaboratory de l’Université de Toronto. Les équipes de @SpaceX ont réalisé le premier test cryogénique du #Ship43 sur le site d’essais de Massey. Ce vaisseau devrait être utilisé lors de l'IFT-16, si tout se passe bien. Samedi 24 octobre Une fusée Falcon 9 de @SpaceX a décollé à 00h48 (heure de Paris) depuis le pas de tir SLC-4E, à Vandenberg, en Californie, pour la mission Starlink 15-15. Sous sa coiffe se trouvaient 27 satellites destinés à la constellation @Starlink. Les équipes de @SpaceX ont procédé à un deuxième test cryogénique du #Ship43 sur le site d’essais de Massey. Dimanche 25 octobre Les équipes de @SpaceX ont réalisé un essai d’allumage statique des 33 moteurs Raptor du booster B22, depuis le pas de tir B du site de lancement de Starbase, au Texas. Le test a duré environ 15 secondes. Pour rappel, le booster B22 devrait être associé au #Ship42 lors du vol d’essai intégré IFT-15, qui pourrait avoir lieu en novembre, au plus tôt. Images : #JAXA / #SpaceX / #RocketLab
